Question: How much does it cost to start?
Answer: Initial costs: Shopify $1 trial then $29-39/month, Printify free (pay per order), Canva free or $13/month for Pro, domain $14/year, email marketing (Klaviyo) free up to 250 subscribers. Total startup: ~$50-100 to launch, then ~$50-100/month in overhead.

Question: Do I need an LLC before starting?
Answer: No. Start as a sole proprietor using your SSN. Once you're consistently making $1,000+/month, consider forming an LLC. You can set one up through services like Incfile for $0-50 + state fees.

Question: How long does setup take?
Answer: Full setup takes 2-4 hours if done in one sitting. Most students break it into 3-4 sessions over a week. You can launch your store in as little as one day if focused.

Question: Can I change my niche/brand name later?
Answer: Yes! Nothing is permanent. The brand name, logo, and even niche can all change. Action over perfection. Many successful brands started with different names (Amazon was originally 'Cadabra').

Question: What if I'm not good at design?
Answer: You don't need design skills. The course provides AI tools (Design GPT, Design Gem) that create professional designs for you. You're not an artist - you're a brand builder creating products people want to buy.

Question: How do I choose the right niche?
Answer: Use Brand Builder GPT to validate ideas. Good niches: (1) You can connect with it personally, (2) Large enough market (GPT verifies this), (3) Not too broad (everyone) or too narrow (nobody). Think: golf, hiking, nursing, dog owners, camping, etc.

Question: What makes a brand different from a generic POD store?
Answer: A brand has: (1) Clear mission/why (Simon Sinek approach), (2) Consistent voice and values, (3) Target audience that feels connected, (4) Repeat customers who come back for new drops. Generic stores just sell random designs with no cohesion.

Question: Can I sell to multiple niches?
Answer: Not recommended for your first brand. Focus on ONE niche to build a loyal audience. Once profitable, you can launch a second brand in a different niche. Spreading too thin kills momentum.

Question: How many designs should I create?
Answer: Start with 100 designs. Launch with 10 in your mockup test, then use catalog ads to test all 100. The more designs you test, the more winners you'll find. Aim to add 20-50 new designs monthly.

Question: What makes a good vs bad design?
Answer: Good: Lots of negative space (t-shirt shows through), 1-3 colors max, easy to read from distance, clear message, emotionally resonant. Bad: Big blocky ink, too many colors, hard-to-read text, looks like AI slop, too complex. Download the 'Good vs Bad Design PDF' from School Community.

Question: How long does it take to create 100 designs?
Answer: Using Design GPT and Design Gem: 4-8 hours total. Work in batches of 10-20. Don't try to perfect everything - good enough is good enough. The goal is to TEST designs, not create art.

Question: Can I use Etsy designs as inspiration?
Answer: Yes, for INSPIRATION only. Never copy/paste designs. Screenshot winning designs on Etsy, analyze patterns (text styles, humor, colors), then create your own unique versions. This is research, not theft.

Question: Should designs be text-based or graphic-based?
Answer: Both! Test variety: 40% text-only (typography), 40% text + graphic, 20% graphic-heavy. Text-based designs often perform best because they're easy to test variations and clearly communicate the message.

Question: What if my designs don't sell?
Answer: Most designs won't be winners - that's expected. Out of 100 designs, you might find 5-10 winners. Turn off losers after $50-100 spend with no sales. Keep creating new designs based on winner patterns.

Question: Which t-shirt provider should I use?
Answer: Gildan 64000, Bella+Canvas or Comfort Colors through Printify. These are premium quality, soft, and have good reviews. Avoid cheap alternatives - quality matters for repeat customers.

Question: How should I price my products?
Answer: Formula: Base cost × 2.5-3 = Your price. Example: $10 base cost = $25-30 retail. Aim for 40%+ profit margin after all fees. Test $27.99, $32.99, $37.99 - higher prices often convert better (more perceived value).

Question: How many shirt colors should I offer?
Answer: Start with 4-8 colors per design. Popular choices: Black, White, Navy, Heather Gray. Let data tell you which colors sell, then add more. Too many options can overwhelm customers.

Question: Should I offer other products besides t-shirts?
Answer: Start with t-shirts only. Once profitable, expand to hoodies, sweatshirts, hats, mugs, etc. But master one product first before diversifying.

Question: How do I make my store look professional?
Answer: Use Build My POD theme (included), upload high-quality mockups (not flat Printify images), write compelling descriptions (use Email GPT + Claude), add trust badges, optimize for mobile, ensure fast load times (<3 seconds).

Question: Do I need a custom domain?
Answer: Yes. yourstore.myshopify.com looks unprofessional. Buy yourbrand.com ($14/year through Shopify or external registrar). .com, .co, .store all work equally well. Also set up support@yourbrand.com for credibility.

Question: How does order fulfillment work?
Answer: Fully automatic: (1) Customer orders on Shopify, (2) Order auto-sends to Printify, (3) Printify prints and ships directly to customer, (4) Customer receives tracking. You never touch inventory. Typical fulfillment: 5-7 business days.

Question: What are shipping costs?
Answer: Printify charges $4-6 shipping per item (varies by product/location). You can charge customers $4.87 flat rate or offer free shipping over $50 (increases average order value). Build shipping cost into your pricing.

Question: What if a customer wants a refund?
Answer: Handle case-by-case. Printify's policy: No refunds for customer mistakes, but they reprint for quality issues. Be generous with refunds for your brand reputation. Budget 1-3% of revenue for refunds/replacements.

Question: How do I handle customer service?
Answer: Set up support@yourbrand.com. Respond within 24 hours. Common questions: Where's my order? (provide tracking), What's your return policy? (link to policy), Sizing questions (provide size chart). Once scaling, hire a VA for $5-8/hour.

Question: How much should I spend on ads to start?
Answer: Mockup Test: $10/day ($10/day × 10 ads) for 2-3 days = $20-30 total. Catalog Ads: Start at $12.50/day once mockup test identifies winners.

Question: What's a good cost per click (CPC)?
Answer: Target: Under $0.75 (great: $0.50-0.75, acceptable: $0.75-1.00, needs work: over $1.00). If CPC is high, improve ad creative (better mockups), test different copy, or adjust targeting.

Question: What's a good ROAS (Return on Ad Spend)?
Answer: Target: 2.5+ ROAS for profitability. Formula: Revenue ÷ Ad Spend. Example: $250 revenue ÷ $100 ad spend = 2.5 ROAS. Under 2.0 ROAS = losing money (after product costs and fees). 3.0+ ROAS = very profitable.

Question: How long until I see results from ads?
Answer: Learning phase: 24-48 hours (algorithm learning). Expect few/no sales initially. Real data: After $200-300 spend. Profitable: After $500-1000 spend you'll know if it's working. Give campaigns 3-7 days before major changes.

Question: What if my ads get rejected?
Answer: Common reasons: (1) Too much text in image (keep under 20%), (2) Misleading claims in copy, (3) Incorrect targeting for ad type. Fix the issue noted in rejection reason and republish. Usually approved within hours.

Question: Mockup test vs Catalog ads - what's the difference?
Answer: Mockup Test: Test 1 specific design with 10 custom mockups ($10/day for 2-3 days). Finds your #1 winner. Catalog Ads: Facebook auto-tests all 100+ products ($12.50/day ongoing). Both needed - mockup test first, then catalog ads.

Question: When should I scale my ads?
Answer: Scale when: (1) 3+ days of consistent 2.5+ ROAS, (2) Cost per purchase under $15, (3) At least 10 purchases tracked. Scale slowly: Increase budget 20% every 3 days. Going too fast can destabilize campaigns.

Question: Do I really need email marketing?
Answer: Yes! Email = repeat customers and higher lifetime value. Your first sale comes from ads, but sales 2, 3, 4+ come from email. Stores with email make 30-40% more revenue than ad-only stores.

Question: What discount should I offer in my popup?
Answer: 15% off (WELCOME15 code) is standard and effective. Delivered immediately in welcome email. Don't go higher than 15% for first purchase - you need margin. Repeat customers can get 10% (LOYAL10).

Question: How many emails should I send?
Answer: Flows (automated): Welcome (3 emails), Abandoned Cart (3 emails), Post-Purchase (4 emails). Campaigns (manual): 1-2 per month for new product drops or promotions. Don't over-email - quality over quantity.

Question: What's a good email open rate?
Answer: Industry average: 15-25% open rate, 1-3% click rate. If below 15%, improve subject lines (use Email GPT) or clean your list (remove inactive subscribers). Higher open rates = better deliverability.

Question: How much profit should I expect per sale?
Answer: Example: $32.99 sale price, minus $10 product cost, minus $5 shipping, minus $1.25 payment fees (2.9% + $0.30), minus $10 ad cost = $6.74 profit (20% margin). Aim for 15-25% profit margins.

Question: When will I break even on my investment?
Answer: If you invest $500 (setup + initial ad spend), you need $2,500 in revenue at 20% margins to break even. Timeline varies: Some break even in 2-3 weeks, others take 2-3 months. Average: 4-8 weeks to profitability.

Question: How much can I realistically make?
Answer: Year 1 realistic goals: $3K-10K/month revenue ($500-2K/month profit). By month 6-12 if you execute well. Year 2: $10K-30K/month revenue with proper scaling. Eric's brands: $850K revenue in a year (SlothHikingClub).

Question: What are all the monthly costs?
Answer: Shopify: $29-39, Klaviyo: $0-100 (scales with subscribers), Facebook Ads: $1,500-3,000+ (this is your investment), Domain: $1.17/month ($14/year), Apps/Tools: $0-50. Total overhead: $50-200/month + ad spend.

Question: My conversion rate is under 1% - what do I do?
Answer: Fix: (1) Better product images (replace Printify flats with mockups), (2) Compelling descriptions (use Email GPT + Claude), (3) Test pricing ($27 vs $32 vs $37), (4) Add trust badges, (5) Improve mobile experience, (6) Simplify checkout.

Question: I'm getting clicks but no sales - why?
Answer: Reasons: (1) Designs aren't resonating (test more), (2) Pricing too high (test lower), (3) Store looks unprofessional (optimize), (4) Shipping cost too high (offer free over $50), (5) Wrong audience (adjust targeting). Review your conversion rate in Shopify Analytics.

Question: My Facebook Pixel isn't firing - help!
Answer: Solutions: (1) Download Meta Pixel Helper Chrome extension, (2) Visit your store and check if pixel shows green, (3) If not, reinstall 'Facebook & Instagram by Meta' app from Shopify, (4) Verify pixel is selected in app settings, (5) Wait 30 minutes and test again.

Question: My catalog ads aren't spending - what's wrong?
Answer: Reasons: (1) Products not synced to catalog yet (takes 1-2 hours after upload), (2) Products missing required fields (price, image, description), (3) Budget too low (minimum $20/day for catalog), (4) Audience too narrow (expand targeting).

Question: I can't connect my domain - DNS issues
Answer: Solution: (1) If using external registrar (GoDaddy, Namecheap), copy exact A and CNAME records from Shopify, (2) Add to DNS settings (NOT forwarding settings), (3) Wait 24-48 hours for propagation, (4) If still not working after 48 hours, contact registrar support.

Question: When should I launch new products?
Answer: Monthly cadence: Launch 20-50 new designs every 30 days. Follow patterns from your winners. Email your list about 'new drops' with NEWDROP10 discount code. Keep fresh products flowing to maintain momentum.

Question: Should I expand to other platforms (Amazon, Etsy)?
Answer: Not initially. Master Shopify + Facebook ads first. Once you're making $5K+/month consistently (3+ months), then consider expanding to Amazon Merch, Etsy, or Google Shopping as additional channels.

Question: When should I hire help?
Answer: Hire when: (1) Consistently profitable 3+ months, (2) Making $5K+/month revenue, (3) You're overwhelmed with tasks. Hire in this order: (1) Designer for new designs, (2) VA for product uploads, (3) VA for customer service, (4) Social media manager.

Question: What should I NOT outsource?
Answer: Keep these in-house: (1) Ad strategy and budget decisions, (2) Email marketing strategy, (3) Brand voice and messaging, (4) Financial tracking and profit analysis, (5) Major strategic decisions. You need to understand your business fundamentals.

Question: Do I need Canva Pro?
Answer: Recommended. Canva Pro ($13/month) gives you 'Remove Background' feature which is essential for cleaning up designs and creating transparent logos. Free version works but Pro makes life much easier.

Answer: All templates are in the WeScale School Community (free to join). Navigate to Classroom → Course → Resources. You'll find: Policy templates, Email flow templates, Product description guide, Good vs Bad Design PDF.

Question: Can I use this with Etsy or Amazon instead of Shopify?
Answer: Not recommended. This course is built specifically for Shopify + Printify + Facebook Ads. Etsy has different dynamics (SEO-focused, high competition, lower margins). Amazon Merch is print-only, no custom store. Stick with Shopify.

Question: How much time does this require per week?
Answer: Launch phase: 10-15 hours/week for 2-4 weeks (setup + first campaigns). Maintenance phase: 5-10 hours/week (checking ads, fulfilling orders, customer service, creating new designs). Scale phase: 15-20 hours/week (or hire help).

Question: What if I've never run a business before?
Answer: Perfect! This course assumes zero business experience. Everything is taught step-by-step. Many successful students had never: (1) Built a website, (2) Run ads, (3) Created designs, (4) Sold anything online. You'll learn it all.

Question: I'm not tech-savvy - can I still do this?
Answer: Yes. If you can use email and browse websites, you can do this. Every tool is explained. Build My POD automates 80% of technical setup. When stuck, use the support resources: WeScale School Community, coach calls, 24/7 Build My POD support.

Question: What's the #1 reason people fail at POD?
Answer: Quitting too early. They spend $200 on ads, get no sales, and quit. Reality: You need $500-1,000 in ad spend to find winners and dial in your system. Give it 30-60 days of consistent effort before deciding it's not working.

Question: Do I need to show my face or build a personal brand?
Answer: No. Your brand is the business (SlothHikingClub, Slice Club, etc), not you personally. You never need to show your face, create content as yourself, or build a following. This is an anonymous, asset-building business model.
